# Singletons reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/singletons/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [GameModeSingleton](#gamemodesingleton)
- [NavMarkerManager](#navmarkermanager)
- [NetworkSessionSingleton](#networksessionsingleton)
- [TickDriverSingleton](#tickdriversingleton)

## GameModeSingleton

`res://assets/scripts/singletons/GameMode.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The shell of the game's rules: holds the game's modules. Autoload "GameMode".

It does almost nothing itself, so an empty one costs nothing and each piece of a game's rules can be swapped or left out. The modules to start come from the project setting `MODULES_SETTING` (script paths, with a ".release" override for release builds), else `DEFAULT_MODULES`; an empty list starts none. A path that doesn't load, or a second module of one type, warns and is skipped.

```gdscript
GameMode.pawn_initializer        # a module, or null if this game doesn't have it, so check first
GameMode.get_module(SomeScript)  # any module by its script
GameMode.add_module(node)        # a game's own modules, which extend GameModeModule
```

### Settings and properties

- `ai_activation_manager: AIActivationManager` = `null`: The module that switches AI pawns off, or null without one. Each module fills in its own line when it starts.
- `possession_coordinator: PossessionCoordinator` = `null`: Who controls which pawn, or null without one.
- `pawn_initializer: PawnInitializer` = `null`: Gives pawns their default parts, or null without one.
- `spawn_manager: SpawnManager` = `null`: Spawns pawns at spawn points and brings players back, or null without one.
- `replay_recorder: ReplayRecorder` = `null`: Records the game to replay files, or null without one (docs/replay/REPLAY_SPEC.md).
- `team_registry: TeamRegistry` = `null`: How many pawns are on each team, or null without one.
- `crowd_mover: CrowdMover` = `null`: Moves AI pawns walking on the ground as one crowd (pawn spec 8.22), or null without one.

### Signals

- `module_added(module: GameModeModule)`: Sent when a module has started.
- `module_removed(module: GameModeModule)`: Sent when a module has stopped, just before it's freed.

### Constants

- `MODULES_SETTING = "project_base/game_mode/modules"`: The project setting that lists the modules to start, as script paths.
- `DEFAULT_MODULES = Array[String](["res://assets/scripts/game_mode/PawnInitializer.gd", "res://assets/scripts/game_mode/PossessionCoordinator.gd", "res://assets/scripts/game_mode/AIActivationManager.gd", "res://assets/scripts/game_mode/SpawnManager.gd", "res://assets/scripts/replay/ReplayRecorder.gd", "res://assets/scripts/game_mode/TeamRegistry.gd", "res://assets/scripts/movement/CrowdMover.gd", "res://assets/scripts/ai/AIDecisionModule.gd"])`: The modules started when the project setting isn't there, in this order.

### Functions

- `add_module(module: GameModeModule) -> void`: Starts a module. It stays until `remove_module()` or until the game ends.
- `remove_module(module: GameModeModule) -> void`: Stops a module and frees it. Anything using it should check again, because it's gone.
- `get_module(script: Script) -> GameModeModule`: The module made from this script, or null if there isn't one.
- `get_modules() -> GameModeModule[]`: Every module right now. Read it, don't change it.

## NavMarkerManager

`res://assets/scripts/singletons/NavMarkerManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Holds every nav marker and answers searches for them. Autoload "NavMarkerManager".

It stores every nav marker, gives each a stable id, and answers searches such as "the nearest point.cover within 20 m". It needs no C++ library, keeps the list of marker modules and tells them when markers change. It doesn't find paths (NavServer) or decide what a pawn does (AI). Requests apply on the next tick; searches return ids and read the state as of the last tick.

```gdscript
var id := NavMarkerManager.find_nearest(&"point.cover", pawn.global_position, 20.0)   # 0: none
var marker := NavMarkerManager.get_marker(id)                                          # the full data, only when needed
```

Design: nav spec 21.5. How it stores markers and searches fast: the README.

### Settings and properties

- `report_unhandled: bool` = `<unknown>`: Whether the debug report runs (debug builds only): it warns once per marker type no module handles. Starts from `REPORT_SETTING`.
- `report_quiet_seconds: float` = `2.0`: How long registrations must stay quiet before the report runs, since a module may just not have arrived yet.

### Constants

- `REPORT_SETTING = "project_base/nav/report_unhandled_markers"`: The project setting that switches the debug report on or off (on by default).
- `CELL_SIZE = 32.0`: How wide each search cell is, in metres. Too small makes wide searches visit many cells, and too large makes each cell hold many markers.
- `NO_ROW = -1`: Means "no row", at the end of a linked list.
- `FNV_OFFSET = -3750763034362895579`
- `FNV_PRIME = 1099511628211`
- `Op.ADD = 0`
- `Op.REMOVE = 1`
- `Op.SET_ENABLED = 2`
- `Op.ADD_MODULE = 3`

### Functions

- `register_terrain(scene_path: String, settings: TerrainSettings) -> int`: A generator registers a copy of its settings and gets the terrain id for its chunks' markers. The id comes from the generator's scene path, so it matches on every machine and across reloads; moving or renaming the node changes it. Registering again replaces the settings.
- `unregister_terrain(terrain: int) -> void`: Forgets a terrain's settings. Its chunks' markers leave through release_markers, not this.
- `get_terrain_settings(terrain: int) -> TerrainSettings`: A registered terrain's settings, or null if there's no such terrain.
- `chunk_of(terrain: int, position: Vector3) -> Vector2i`: Which chunk a position in the world is in, whether or not that chunk is loaded. Vector2i.ZERO for an unknown terrain.
- `request_markers(terrain: int, chunk: Vector2i, markers: NavMarker[]) -> int`: A chunk announces its markers. Returns how many were accepted; refused ones get one warning between them. A marker's id comes from its place in this list, so a generator must build the list the same way every time.
- `request_scene_marker(scene_path: String, marker: NavMarker) -> int`: A hand-placed marker asks to be registered. Returns its id, or 0 if refused. NavMarkerNode calls this with its scene path, so moving or renaming that node changes the id.
- `release_markers(terrain: int, chunk: Vector2i) -> void`: A chunk is unloading, so all its markers leave. Changes made to them are kept for when it comes back.
- `remove_scene_marker(id: int) -> void`: Removes one hand-placed marker. A chunk's markers leave through release_markers instead.
- `set_enabled(id: int, enabled: bool) -> void`: Switches a marker on or off. A chunk marker's change is remembered through unloads, only while it differs from how the marker started, so memory doesn't grow with the world.
- `flush() -> void`: Applies every waiting request now, and tells modules. The tick does this by itself; tests and tools can call it directly.
- `add_module(module: NavMarkerModule) -> void`: A module entered the tree. It joins on the next tick, so its own _ready has run by the time it gets any calls.
- `remove_module(module: NavMarkerModule) -> void`: A module is leaving the tree. This happens at once, not next tick, as the module may not exist by then. It gets a final _markers_removed so it can undo its work. The markers stay registered.
- `reset() -> void`: Forgets every marker and kept change. For tests and leaving a level. Modules stay and are told their markers are gone; modules waiting to join still join next tick.
- `get_unhandled_types() -> Dictionary`: Types with markers that no module announced, as type name -> how many markers. This is what the debug report warns about.
- `get_automatic_report_count() -> int`: How many automatic reports have been made since the last reset.
- `print_report() -> void`: Prints the unhandled types on demand, in any build.
- `_type_is_claimed(type_index: int) -> bool`: True if a module that counts for the report handles this type.
- `find_nearest(tag: StringName, from: Vector3, max_distance: float) -> int`: The id of the nearest enabled marker matching the tag, within max_distance. 0 if there's none. Equal distances go to the lower id, so every machine picks the same marker.
- `find_in_radius(tag: StringName, from: Vector3, radius: float) -> PackedInt64Array`: The ids of every enabled marker matching the tag, within the radius. Sorted by id, so every machine gets the same order.
- `get_marker(id: int) -> NavMarker`: The full data for a marker, or null if there's no such id.
- `get_marker_position(id: int) -> Vector3`: Where a marker is. Vector3.ZERO if there's no such id.
- `is_marker_enabled(id: int) -> bool`: True if this marker is on. False for an unknown id.
- `get_marker_count() -> int`: How many markers are registered, applied or waiting for the next tick.
- `get_pending_count() -> int`: How many requests are waiting for the next tick.
- `get_kept_change_count() -> int`: How many marker changes are being remembered for chunks, loaded or not.
- `chunk_marker_id(terrain: int, chunk: Vector2i, index: int) -> int`: The same chunk and index give the same id on every machine, and after every reload.
- `scene_marker_id(scene_path: String) -> int`: A hand-placed marker's id, from its scene path: the same on every machine, and after every reload.
- `fnv_hash(bytes: PackedByteArray) -> int`: The FNV-1a hash of some bytes: for each byte, XOR it in and multiply by the prime. Relies on 64-bit ints wrapping. Written out here because Godot's hash() could differ from a C++ version.
- `_why_refused(marker: NavMarker, id: int) -> String`: Why a marker can't be registered, or "" if it can.
- `_write_row(marker: NavMarker, id: int, from_chunk: bool) -> int`: Fills a row and returns its number. The marker isn't searchable until _link_row runs on the next tick.
- `_type_index_of(script: Script) -> int`: The number for a marker's type, adding the type the first time it's seen.
- `_find_modules_for(script: Script) -> Array`: Every joined module that handles this type or one of its parents.
- `_ids_handled_by(module: NavMarkerModule) -> PackedInt64Array`: The ids of every applied marker this module handles. It checks every row, so it's only for joining and leaving.
- `_tell_modules(rows: PackedInt32Array, what: int) -> void`: Gives each module one call, with the ids it handles out of these rows.
- `_link_row(row: int) -> void`: Puts a row at the front of its cell's linked list, which is what makes it searchable.
- `_unlink_row(row: int) -> void`: Takes a row out of its cell's linked list by joining its two neighbours to each other.
- `_cell_of(position: Vector3) -> Vector2i`: Which cell a position is in. Height doesn't matter: the world is a flat plane with layers on it.
- `_search_bit(tag: StringName) -> int`: The tag's bit for searching, or 0 if nothing can match it. Never adds a tag.
- `_cells_in_ring(center: Vector2i, ring: int) -> Array`: The square ring of cells exactly this many cells away from the center.
- `_cells_within(from: Vector3, radius: float) -> Array`: Every cell a search of this radius has to look at, or just the occupied ones if that's fewer.

## NetworkSessionSingleton

`res://assets/scripts/singletons/NetworkSession.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The multiplayer session (autoload "NetworkSession"): connects machines, spawns entities on all of them, and moves inputs and snapshots between them. Offline it does nothing and entities play as single player.

The standard model for competitive action games: the server is the authority and clients send it inputs only; a client runs ahead so its input for tick T arrives before the server runs T; its own pawn is predicted and corrected (reconciliation); everything else is drawn in the past between snapshots (interpolation); the server checks attacks (LagCompensation). It all runs inside TickDriver's ticks. Non-entity systems, such as terrain edits, send their own messages through world and client channels.

```gdscript
NetworkSession.register_type("pawn", preload("res://pawn.tscn"))  # same types in the same order on every machine
NetworkSession.world_root = $Entities
NetworkSession.host(port)   # or NetworkSession.join(address, port)
NetworkSession.spawn("pawn", peer_id, Vector3(0, 1, 0))   # on the server; a joining player spawns nothing by itself
```

Design: netcode spec 4, 6, 10, 11. Tick order, packet formats, time dilation and the rules: the README.

### Settings and properties

- `snapshot_rate: int` = `30`: Snapshots per second. A server's entities save state only on snapshot ticks (NetworkEntity.refresh_input_saving), so changing this tells them.
- `interpolation_seconds: float` = `0.1`: How far in the past remote entities are drawn. Enough to always have two snapshots to blend between.
- `max_interpolation_seconds: float` = `0.2`: The most the adaptive version may draw in the past. Also limits how far back a client may claim to see.
- `lead_margin_ticks: int` = `3`: Extra ticks of lead beyond half the round trip, so input still arrives on time when the connection wobbles.
- `resync_threshold_ticks: int` = `4`: How far from its lead a client can drift before it jumps back, with dilation off.
- `resync_threshold_with_dilation_ticks: int` = `15`: How far ahead of its lead a client can drift before it jumps back, with dilation on. Dilation corrects gently, so this only covers things too big for that.
- `resync_behind_with_dilation_ticks: int` = `6`: With dilation on, being behind is treated more urgently than being ahead: a tick behind is an input lost.
- `dilation_margin_low_ticks: int` = `1`: Inputs should arrive at least this many ticks early. Below this in the last half second, the client speeds up.
- `dilation_margin_high_ticks: int` = `2`: If even the worst of the last 5 seconds is above this, the client is further ahead than it needs to be, and slows down.
- `dilation_gain: float` = `0.02`: How much to change speed per tick outside that range. Low enough not to overshoot on a late answer.
- `dilation_max_speedup: float` = `0.05`: The fastest a client will run, as a fraction above normal speed. A few percent isn't noticeable.
- `dilation_max_slowdown: float` = `0.03`: The slowest a client will run, as a fraction below normal speed.
- `prediction_enabled: bool` = `true`: Your own pawn reacts at once and gets corrected. Off: it waits for the server, so what you do shows up after your ping.
- `reconciliation_enabled: bool` = `true`: Your own pawn is corrected when the server disagrees. Off: it drifts, which shows what prediction alone would do.
- `interpolation_enabled: bool` = `true`: Remote entities are drawn in the past between snapshots. Off: they jump to each newest snapshot.
- `extrapolation_enabled: bool` = `true`: Remote entities move on from the newest snapshot if nothing newer has arrived. Off: they hold.
- `correction_smoothing_enabled: bool` = `true`: The visible model hides a correction's jump. Off: you see the jump.
- `follow_during_rollback: bool` = `false`: During a rollback, remote entities stand on server data rather than where they're drawn. See TickStateComponent.
- `time_dilation_enabled: bool` = `true`: A client's lead follows its connection. Off: it's set once, and jumps back when it drifts.
- `adaptive_interpolation_enabled: bool` = `true`: More jitter draws remote entities further in the past. Off: always interpolation_seconds.
- `delta_snapshots_enabled: bool` = `true`: Snapshots send each entity's changes since its baseline for that client: the newest snapshot whose part holding it the client acknowledged reading (per-part ACKs), instead of everything. Off: every entity in full, to compare.
- `rewind_cap_seconds: float` = `0.35`: How far back lag compensation may go. At 200 ms ping a shooter sees others about 350 ms behind its own tick (round trip, margin and interpolation), so this covers that and not much more. Past it, players have to lead their shots.
- `lag_compensation_enabled: bool` = `true`: Turns lag compensation off, to compare.
- `default_predicted: bool` = `false`: Project default for is_predicted on every entity. Entities can also turn it on for themselves.
- `input_redundancy: int` = `3`: How many inputs each input packet carries, the newest and some past ones, in case some are lost. Each extra one adds about 1.7 KB/s of upload. At 3, three packets in a row must be lost for an input to go missing.
- `missing_input_hold_ticks: int` = `3`: On the server, when a client's input goes missing, the last one repeats in full for this many ticks. Most losses are a tick or two. An entity can use its own number instead; Pawn has missing_input_hold_ticks for that.
- `missing_input_fade_ticks: int` = `6`: Then its direction fades to nothing over this many ticks, so a pawn whose player lost connection doesn't walk on forever. Pawn can override it with missing_input_fade_ticks.
- `use_native_encoding: bool` = `true`: Snapshots go through NetCodec in C++ when that library is here. Off, or with no library for this platform, they go through NetPackets instead. The bytes are the same, so machines of either kind can play together. Takes effect at host or join.
- `world_root: Node` = `null`: Where spawned entities go. Defaults to the current scene.
- `bind_address: String` = `"*"`: Which address the server listens on. "*" is all of them.
- `max_packets_per_second: int` = `2000`: Server: most packets one client may send a second, so a broken or hostile client can't bury the server. Over it, `max_bytes_per_second` or `max_packet_bytes`, packets are dropped and counted in stats (0: no limit). A pawn costs a client about 60 packets and 6 KB a second.
- `max_bytes_per_second: int` = `262144`: Server: the most bytes one client may send a second. See `max_packets_per_second`.
- `max_packet_bytes: int` = `65536`: Server: the largest packet a client may send. See `max_packets_per_second`.
- `packet_filter: Object` = `null`: Something that can hold packets back on their way out and in, or null, which is normal. NetDebugModule fills it with its fake network. It has hold_outgoing(peer, bytes, reliable), hold_incoming(peer, bytes), release_due(now_usec) and clear().
- `stats: Dictionary` = `{...}`: Bytes, packets and more, for diagnostics. A server counts snapshots_sent and snapshot_bytes (one per client per snapshot); a client snapshot_bytes_received, snapshot_parts_received and deltas_without_baseline; both the largest packet each way.
- `render_tick: float` = `-1.0`: Client: which tick of the server's remote entities are being drawn at. -1 before the first snapshot.
- `server_load_percent: int` = `-1`: Client: how loaded the server's ticks are, as a percentage of their budget (TickDriver.load_average), from the newest snapshot. -1 before the first. The samples' status line shows it, for profiling different hardware.
- `server_load_step: int` = `-1`: Client: the server's load ladder step (TickDriver.load_step), from the newest snapshot. -1 before the first.

### Signals

- `hosted()`: Server: hosting has started.
- `joined()`: Client: connected, past the handshake, and ticking.
- `refused(reason: String)`: Client: couldn't join, and why.
- `disconnected()`: The connection ended; `connection_ended` was sent just before, with the reason.
- `player_connected(peer: int)`: Server: a client passed the handshake.
- `player_leaving(peer: int)`: Server: a client has gone, and what it owns hasn't been removed yet, so a listener can keep something by giving it a new owner.
- `player_left(peer: int)`: Server: a client has gone, and what it owned has been removed.
- `entity_spawned(entity: NetworkEntity)`: An entity was made on this machine, by spawn or a spawn packet.
- `entity_despawned(entity_id: int)`: An entity was removed on this machine.
- `entity_owner_changed(entity: NetworkEntity)`: An entity has a new owner, on every machine.
- `connection_ended(peer: int, reason: String, details: Dictionary)`: A connection ended, and why, for diagnostics. peer is 1 on a client (sent just before `disconnected`); on a server, once per client that goes, and 0 when the server stops. details: seconds_connected, seconds_since_heard, rtt_ms, loss_percent (-1: never measured).

### Constants

- `Mode.OFFLINE = 0`
- `Mode.SERVER = 1`
- `Mode.CLIENT = 2`
- `SERVER_FEATURES = Array[String](["lag_compensation_enabled", "default_predicted"])`: The settings the server decides for everyone, so snapshots say what they are.
- `NO_MARGIN = 32767`: What snapshots say when a client has sent no input lately.
- `MARGIN_SHORT_WINDOW = 30`: How many recent input packets count for the quick check that speeds up: half a second at 60 a second.
- `MARGIN_LONG_WINDOW = 300`: How many recent input packets count for the slow check that slows down: 5 seconds at 60 a second.
- `COUNTING_STATS = Array[String](["bytes_sent", "bytes_received", "snapshots_encoded", "snapshots_sent", "snapshot_bytes", "snapshots_received", "snapshot_bytes_received", "corrections", "resyncs", "interpolation_underruns"])`: The stats that only ever count up, which diagnostics turns into rates and averages per frame. Renaming one here renames it there, since diagnostics names none of them itself.
- `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT = 5.0`: Seconds a new connection has to pass the handshake before the server drops it.
- `SAMPLES_BEFORE_TICKING = 6`: Pongs a client waits for before it sets its clock and starts ticking.
- `PING_INTERVAL_STARTING = 0.05`: Seconds between a client's pings while it's setting its clock.
- `PING_INTERVAL = 0.25`: Seconds between a client's pings once its clock is set.
- `BUILD_ID_SETTING = "project_base/network/build_id"`: The project setting that names a build. See `content_hash()`.
- `HASHED_FILE_TYPES = PackedStringArray("gd", "gdc", "tscn", "scn", "tres", "res")`: The file types `content_hash()` reads when no build id is set.
- `MAX_INBOX_PER_PEER = 128`: Most packets the server keeps from one client between ticks, so one client can't crowd out others. A client sends one per pawn per tick, so 128 holds 4 pawns through a half-second freeze. A client doesn't cap what its server sends (see handle_packet).
- `MAX_INPUTS_PER_PACKET = 16`: Most inputs one packet may carry. Fixed, because input_redundancy is a setting each machine has its own copy of.
- `SNAPSHOT_PART_BYTES = 1100`: Snapshots are split into parts of at most this many bytes of entities, each its own packet, so none goes over ENet's packet size (1392 bytes) and the loss of one piece doesn't lose the whole snapshot.
- `DELTA_ID_BIT = 2147483648`: An entity's id with this bit set means its state list is a delta: [ticks back to the baseline, the change masks, the changed values]. Ids never get this high.
- `DELTA_MASK_BITS = 30`: How many state entries each change mask covers. 30 keeps a mask an int of at most 5 bytes, and 1 or 2 when only the first few entries changed.
- `DELTA_MAX_BASELINE_AGE = 48`: The oldest baseline a delta may use, in ticks. Both sides keep 64 ticks, so this leaves room. A client that hasn't acknowledged anything this recent gets everything in full.
- `BASELINE_RING = 64`: How many ticks of received state a client keeps per entity, for decoding deltas.
- `NET_MONITORS_SCRIPT = "res://assets/scripts/netcode/debug/NetMonitors.gd"`: The debugger graphs' script, loaded only if it's there (see _ready).
- `MAX_ACK_ENTRIES = 8`: The most ticks one ACK packet may name. A client sends at most this many, and the server refuses a packet claiming more, so one packet can't make it walk through a long made-up list.
- `LINK_CHECK_INTERVAL_USEC = 500000`: How often each connection's round trip and packet loss are read from ENet, in microseconds.

### Functions

- `_new_peer(welcomed: bool) -> NetworkSessionSingleton.PeerRecord`: A new client's record. Tests make theirs with this too.
- `register_type(type_name: String, scene: PackedScene) -> void`: Adds a type of entity that can be spawned. Every machine must add the same ones.
- `get_type_scene(type_name: String) -> PackedScene`: The scene registered for this type name, or null. SpawnManager reads a type's team from it.
- `host(port: int, max_clients: int = 32) -> int`: Starts a server. Returns OK or an error.
- `join(address: String, port: int) -> int`: Connects to a server. joined or refused follows later. Returns OK or an error.
- `leave() -> void`: Ends the session and removes everything it spawned. Safe to call at any time.
- `get_mode() -> int`: Whether this machine is offline, a server or a client.
- `is_server() -> bool`: True on a server (a host).
- `get_match_options() -> PackedStringArray`: The settings a start menu may offer before a match (MatchOptionsPanel.add_from_autoloads): the snapshots. The host's decide for everyone.
- `get_newest_snapshot_tick() -> int`: Client: the tick of the newest snapshot that has arrived, -1 before any. How fast it climbs is how fast the server is really ticking, which the samples' status line shows.
- `is_client() -> bool`: True on a client, from join until it leaves.
- `get_local_peer() -> int`: This machine's peer id. Offline, and on the server, it's 1.
- `is_connected_to_session() -> bool`: True while a real connection is up (not offline, and connected).
- `get_rtt_ms() -> float`: Client: the measured round trip in milliseconds.
- `get_lead_ticks() -> float`: Client: how many ticks ahead of the server it's actually running.
- `get_view_ticks_behind() -> float`: Client: how many ticks behind its own tick remote entities are drawn. Attacks send this, for lag compensation.
- `get_tick_factor() -> float`: Client: how fast its ticks are running compared to normal.
- `get_input_margin() -> int`: Client: the worst the server has lately seen its inputs arrive, in ticks early. Negative is late. NO_MARGIN if unknown.
- `get_missed_inputs() -> int`: Client: how many of its inputs the server has had to do without.
- `limit_view_ticks_behind(peer: int, claimed: float, tick: int) -> float`: How many ticks behind its own tick a client can believably be drawing others (lag compensation): no newer than its last acknowledged snapshot, no further behind that than the interpolation limit, and none past the rewind cap. Offline, the host's own pawn and AI aren't limited.
- `content_hash() -> int`: A number that's the same on two machines only if they run the same content; the handshake refuses a client whose differs. It covers the packet format, tag sets, input actions, engine build, physics settings, entity schemas, and the game's files (or `BUILD_ID_SETTING` if set).
- `_add_file_hashes(folder: String, parts: PackedStringArray) -> void`: The name and contents of every script, scene and resource in this folder and below. Folders starting with a dot are skipped: that's Godot's cache, and git's. An exported game has the same kinds of files, in their packed forms.
- `spawn(type_name: String, owner_peer: int, at: Variant) -> Node`: Server or offline: makes an entity on this machine and on every client. owner_peer sends its input; 0 is the server itself.
- `despawn(entity_id: int) -> void`: Server or offline: removes an entity everywhere.
- `set_entity_owner(entity_id: int, new_owner: int) -> void`: Server or offline: gives an entity to another player, or to nobody with 0. Every client hears about it. From then on, its input comes from the new owner, and the new owner's machine predicts it.
- `get_entity(entity_id: int) -> NetworkEntity`: The entity with this id, or null.
- `get_entities() -> NetworkEntity[]`: Every live entity, in id order. The same list each time, rebuilt only when entities come and go, because several per-tick paths use it. Read it, don't change it.
- `refresh_entities() -> void`: A switch changed: every entity works out its role again. NetDebugModule calls it after a feature switch, and a client after the server's features arrive.
- `send_now(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray, reliable: bool) -> void`: Sends bytes straight away, past `packet_filter`. NetDebugModule hands it to its fake network to send what it held back.
- `_on_packet(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Everything arriving comes through here. Connection packets act at once. Inputs and snapshots wait for the next tick, so they're applied at a fixed point in the tick's order.
- `_within_limits(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> bool`: Server: may this client send this packet now? Until it has passed the handshake, it may only send the packet that does that. Every packet counts against the per-second limits, pings included.
- `handle_packet(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray, _reliable: bool) -> void`: Acts on one arrived packet, after `packet_filter`. NetDebugModule hands it to its fake network to deliver what it held back.
- `_drop_silent_peers() -> void`: A client that connected but never finished the handshake, or was refused and stayed.
- `_new_link() -> Dictionary`: A new connection's numbers.
- `_check_links(now: int) -> void`: Every LINK_CHECK_INTERVAL_USEC, each connection's round trip and packet loss as ENet measures them, kept because ENet can't be asked once a connection has gone. Skipped when the peer isn't an ENetMultiplayerPeer (a test's own kind).
- `get_link_stats() -> Dictionary`: Each connection's last known numbers, peer -> {"seconds_connected", "seconds_since_heard", "rtt_ms", "loss_percent"}. On a client the one connection is peer 1, the server. Diagnostics shows these in its summaries.
- `_jump_back_if_drifted() -> void`: Client: jumps the tick back to its target if it has drifted too far. Checked every frame, so a client that froze is back on time at once. The clock goes by the fastest recent ping, so a lag spike doesn't look like falling behind.
- `register_world_channel(channel: String, receive: Callable, catch_up: Callable = Callable()) -> void`: Sets up a channel. receive(bytes) runs on clients. catch_up() runs on the server when a client joins, and returns the bytes to send it, or empty for nothing.
- `unregister_world_channel(channel: String) -> void`: Removes a channel set up with `register_world_channel()`.
- `send_world_message(channel: String, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Server: sends bytes to every client on a channel. Does nothing anywhere else.
- `_on_world_message(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Only a server sends these, so anyone else sending one is misbehaving.
- `register_client_channel(channel: String, receive: Callable) -> void`: Sets up a channel. receive(peer, bytes) runs on the server.
- `unregister_client_channel(channel: String) -> void`: Removes a channel set up with `register_client_channel()`.
- `send_to_server(channel: String, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Client: sends bytes to the server on a channel. Does nothing anywhere else.
- `_profile_part(part: StringName, mark: int) -> int`: Adds the time since mark to one network part of a tick, in the driver's timing record. Returns now, the next part's mark.
- `get_snapshot_interval() -> int`: Ticks between snapshots: a server sends one when the tick is a multiple of this. 1 without a tick driver.
- `_send_inputs(tick: int) -> void`: Client: sends this tick's input for each entity it controls, plus a few past ones in case some were lost.
- `_send_part_acks() -> void`: Client: says which snapshot parts it has read since the last time, one ACK packet a tick at most: type, count u8 (up to 8, newest first), then per tick its tick u32, part count u8 and a bit per part (1: read, every entity in it). Unreliable: a lost ACK only keeps older baselines in use.
- `_note_part_read(tick: int, part: int, part_count: int) -> void`: Client: notes that it read a part of a snapshot, every entity in it, for the next ACK.
- `_on_ack(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Server: a client says which parts of which snapshots it read. Each entity in a read part gets that tick as its baseline for this client if newer. Unknown parts and future ticks are ignored. It also counts for lag compensation (only moves forward).
- `_on_input(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray, tick: int) -> void`: Server: stores a client's inputs for the ticks they belong to. Only the owner may send them, and they're cleaned first.
- `_margins_to_report(info: NetworkSessionSingleton.PeerRecord, tick: int) -> PackedInt32Array`: Server: the two timing reports for a client's next snapshot: its worst margin over the last half second and over the last 5; NO_MARGIN if unknown. A client silent for the short window (spectating, dead pawn) gets NO_MARGIN for both and its margins are dropped.
- `_note_input_timing(peer: int, newest: int, acknowledged: int, tick: int) -> void`: Server: how early this input packet arrived, for time dilation. Only packets with something new count (a duplicate isn't late input). What a client acknowledges only moves forward, and a client can't have seen the future.
- `_make_codec(expected_protocol: int) -> Object`: NetCodec if it's usable. Falls back to NetPackets if the library is missing, or was built for another packet format and would need rebuilding. Asking for it by name means this script still runs on a platform without the library.
- `is_using_native_encoding() -> bool`: True if snapshots are going through C++ right now.
- `_is_in_snapshot(entity: NetworkEntity, tick: int) -> bool`: Whether an entity goes in this tick's snapshot: it does if it recorded this tick, even with no state list (only save_state() data or sync properties). A paused entity records nothing, so it's left out.
- `_send_snapshots(tick: int) -> void`: Server: sends the world to every client, with a note for each on how its input is arriving, for time dilation.
- `_snapshot_entry(entity: NetworkEntity, tick: int, id: int, state_values: Array, state_encodings: Array) -> Array`: One entity's lists for the codec, as write_world takes them, with the given id and state list.
- `_delta_entity_bytes(entity: NetworkEntity, tick: int, baseline: int) -> PackedByteArray`: An entity encoded as its changes since baseline, or empty if it must go in full (no state list, nothing saved for that tick, or a list too long). The state list becomes ticks back, masks, changed values; the id gets `DELTA_ID_BIT`; each mask covers `DELTA_MASK_BITS` entries.
- `delta_state_lists(now: Array, then: Array, encodings: Array, ticks_back: int) -> Array` *(static)*: The change check for a delta: returns the values and encodings to send, laid out as ticks_back, masks, then each changed value. Empty if the lists differ in length or the result is too long. A value is unchanged if type and value match. Twin of NetCodec.delta_state (C++). Static, so it can be called without a session.
- `_cut_into_parts(chunks: PackedByteArray[], ids: PackedInt32Array) -> NetworkSessionSingleton.SnapshotPart[]`: Groups encoded entities into parts of at most SNAPSHOT_PART_BYTES (a bigger one goes alone), with each chunk's entity id in ids. Always at least one part, so an empty snapshot still arrives; at most 255.
- `_apply_server_features(mask: int) -> void`: Client: the features the server decides are whatever it says. default_predicted changes roles, so this matters in a real game too.
- `_on_snapshot(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Client: remote entities store what the snapshot says. Predicted ones keep it aside for _reconcile, newest only.
- `_rebuild_from_delta(entity: NetworkEntity, tick: int, delta: Array) -> Variant`: Client: the full state list from a delta ([ticks back, masks..., changed values]) and what this client kept for that entity at the baseline tick. Null if the baseline isn't here or the delta doesn't fit.
- `_keep_baseline(entity_id: int, tick: int, values: Array) -> void`: Client: keeps what the server sent for an entity on a tick, to decode later deltas against.
- `_reconcile() -> void`: Client: compares predictions with the newest snapshot, and if any are wrong, corrects them and resimulates from there.
- `_move_remote_entities() -> void`: Client: moves the drawing clock on one tick, keeping it a fixed distance behind the newest snapshot, then places every remote entity. It runs slightly fast or slow to catch up rather than jumping, so motion stays smooth.
- `_interpolation_ticks() -> float`: How far behind the newest snapshot to draw. With jitter, snapshots arrive unevenly, so it draws further back to keep having two to blend between.
- `_note_snapshot_timing(tick: int) -> void`: How unevenly snapshots are arriving, as a slow average of how far each is from when it was expected.
- `_update_dilation(margin: int, margin_long: int) -> void`: Client: the server said how early our inputs arrived, at worst, over the last half second and the last 5. Too close over the short one: speed up, more the further out. Plenty to spare over the long one: slow down. Else normal speed; late costs inputs, early only a little.
- `set_tick_factor(factor: float) -> void`: Client: sets how fast its ticks run compared to normal (time dilation), and notes the extremes in stats. NetDebugModule calls it too, to go back to normal speed.

## TickDriverSingleton

`res://assets/scripts/singletons/TickDriver.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Runs all gameplay in numbered, fixed-length ticks, online and offline. Autoload "TickDriver".

Every machine runs it. Pawns, TickStateComponent and NetworkEntity register with it and get called once a tick, in phases, instead
of in their own _physics_process; abilities, AI and netcode all run on it. `dt` is always the fixed tick length.

```gdscript
TickDriver.register(self)   # then write any of _tick_input(dt, tick), _tick_capture_input(tick),
                            # _tick_simulate(dt, tick), _tick_record(tick); each is optional
```

One tick: `before_tick`, input, capture input, simulate, `after_simulate`, record, commit, `after_tick`. Within a
phase, lower `order` runs first, then registration order. The commit writes every entity's state into `store`, the
record of play at tick boundaries. A participant with a `due_tick` property (a pawn) isn't called in input or simulate
before that tick, so a pawn on a load step costs nothing on the ticks it skips. Rollback and the load ladder are in the README.
Design: state store spec 4 and 9, netcode spec 3 (rollback 3.5), scaling spec 7, pawn spec 8.21 (load ladder).

### Settings and properties

- `tick_rate: int` = `0`: Ticks per second; 0 is the project setting, else the physics rate. Fixed before a match (scaling spec 7): clients take the server's in
  the handshake. A dedicated server can set it with `-- --tick-rate=30`.
- `max_ticks_per_frame: int` = `3`: Most ticks one frame may run; the rest of the time is dropped (the game slows down instead of freezing). The autoload sets
  Godot's `max_physics_steps_per_frame` to match, since that limit is the one that really counts.
- `physics_follows_tick_rate: bool` = `true`: On, the autoload sets Godot's physics rate to the tick rate, so there is one tick per physics step. Off, physics keeps the project's
  rate with ticks at another.
- `active: bool` = `true`: False pauses ticking.
- `history_depth: int` = `64`: Ticks of history `store` keeps: the deepest any reader needs (rollback, lag compensation, snapshot baselines). Applies while
  the store is empty, so set it before entities arrive.
- `verify_store_each_tick: bool` = `false`: On, the start of each tick checks every bound entity's nodes still hold what the last commit recorded, and warns about the ones that
  don't: something wrote around the store (state store spec 4). Costs a read of every gathered value; for finding such writes.
- `store: Object` = `null`: The central record of play (`StateStore` in C++, or its twin [`StateStoreGD`](../state_store/REFERENCE.md#statestoregd)): every entity's state at the end of each
  tick. Untyped because it's one of two classes with the same calls.
- `use_native_store: bool` = `true`: Use the C++ store when the library is there. Off: the GDScript twin, for comparing (tests take `-- --gdscript-store`).
- `store_mismatches: int` = `0`: Entities the tripwire (`verify_store_each_tick`) has caught, added up.
- `tick: int` = `0`: Current tick number: the last tick that ran, 0 before any. Change it only with `set_tick()`.
- `tick_factor: float` = `1.0`: Time dilation multiplier: how fast ticks happen. 1.0 offline and on the server; on a client the netcode nudges it to keep its clock right.
- `dropped_ticks: int` = `0`: Ticks dropped by the `max_ticks_per_frame` limit, plus time Godot dropped beyond its own limit; for diagnostics.
- `load_ladder_enabled: bool` = `true`: On, `load_step` follows how loaded the ticks are. Off, it stays at 1 (unless `load_step_override` says otherwise).
- `max_load_step: int` = `4`: The highest `load_step` the ladder goes to: 1, 2 or 4.
- `load_step_override: int` = `0`: 0: automatic. 1, 2 or 4: forced, for testing a level or a game that wants one.
- `raise_above: float` = `0.85`: The share of a tick's budget above which the ladder steps up, after `raise_after_ticks` in a row.
- `raise_after_ticks: int` = `30`: Ticks in a row over `raise_above` before it steps up, at 60 a second. 30: half a second.
- `lower_below: float` = `0.4`: The share of a tick's budget below which the ladder steps down, after `lower_after_ticks` in a row. It also steps down when
  it predicts the lower step fits (`step_down_headroom`), as much of a tick doesn't shrink with the AI's step.
- `step_down_headroom: float` = `0.15`: It also steps down when the load predicted for the lower step is under `raise_above` minus this. Predicted: the load now plus
  what stepping up saved last time; with no measurement yet, twice the load.
- `saving_measured_after_ticks: int` = `30`: Ticks after a step up before the load is measured to work out what it saved, at 60 a second. About three times what the average
  takes to settle.
- `smallest_believable_saving: float` = `0.05`: A measured saving under this share of the budget counts as not measured (the load likely rose for another reason), so stepping down
  assumes the load doubles; this stops the ladder bouncing.
- `lower_after_ticks: int` = `180`: Ticks in a row under `lower_below` (or with the lower step predicted to fit) before it steps down, at 60 a second. 180: three
  seconds.
- `load_step: int` = `1`: The most every AI pawn may run, as a step: 1 every tick, 2 every 2nd, 4 every 4th. Read it; set `load_step_override` to force it.
- `load_average: float` = `0.0`: How much of its budget a tick has used lately, smoothed over about ten ticks: 1.0 is the whole tick's length.
- `profile_enabled: bool` = `false`: On, each tick phase adds up its time in microseconds into `profile`, for finding what's slow. Off, it costs a few flag checks
  per tick.
- `profile: Dictionary` = `{}`: Each phase's time in microseconds, plus the counts in `PROFILE_COUNTS`, while `profile_enabled` is on. Emptied by
  `reset_profile()`.

### Signals

- `before_tick_loop()`: Sent once a frame, before the frame's first tick. Not sent in a frame with no tick due.
- `before_tick(dt: float, tick: int)`: Sent at the start of each tick, before any phase. The netcode applies snapshots here, and may roll back from it.
- `after_tick(dt: float, tick: int)`: Sent at the end of each tick, after every phase. A rollback from here counts this tick as finished.
- `after_simulate(dt: float, tick: int)`: Sent after every participant has simulated, before anything is recorded (pawn spec 15.1). Queued effects, such as hits, are delivered
  here, so they never depend on simulate order. Not sent during a replay.
- `after_tick_loop()`: Sent once a frame, after the frame's last tick. Delays counted in ticks (SpawnManager's, say) run here, between ticks.
- `after_rollback(from_tick: int, to_tick: int)`: Sent when a rollback's replay is over: it went back to from_tick and replayed up to to_tick.
- `rollback_state_loaded(from_tick: int)`: State is back to from_tick and the replay is about to run. A correction can move a pawn here, and anything that must be ready
  before it moves (the ground, say) gets its chance now.
- `load_step_changed(step: int)`: Sent when `load_step` changes (see the load ladder in the README).

### Constants

- `TICK_RATE_SETTING = "project_base/network/tick_rate"`: The project setting for the tick rate. 0 or missing: the project's physics rate.
- `REFERENCE_RATE = 60`: Settings counted in ticks are written for 60 ticks a second, whatever rate a game runs at.
  `ticks_at_rate()` turns one into ticks at this match's rate.
- `PROFILE_COUNTS = Array[String](["ticks", "rollbacks", "rollback_ticks"])`: The entries of `profile` that count things. The rest are times in microseconds.

### Functions

- `register(participant: Object, order: int = 0) -> void`: Adds a participant. `order`: lower runs first within each phase; equal order keeps registration order. Registering twice
  changes nothing; during a tick it takes effect next tick. Gotcha: a participant that also has _physics_process must turn it off in _ready, not _enter_tree, or it ticks twice.
- `replace_store(new_store: Object) -> void`: Swaps in a new, empty store (null: a fresh one of the kind `use_native_store` picks), for tests comparing the two. Entities
  already recorded stay in the old one, so call it before they arrive.
- `unregister(participant: Object) -> void`: Removes a participant. During a tick its calls stop at once (a pawn despawned mid-tick isn't simulated or recorded). Freed ones are dropped by themselves.
- `is_registered(participant: Object) -> bool`: True if this participant is registered.
- `get_participant_count() -> int`: How many participants are registered.
- `advance(elapsed: float) -> void`: Feeds elapsed time in and runs the ticks it covers, at most `max_ticks_per_frame` (the rest is dropped and counted). Called every
  physics frame while `active`; tests call it directly.
- `step() -> void`: Runs exactly one tick now, whatever the time. For tests and tools.
- `get_tick_rate() -> int`: Ticks per second this match runs at.
- `ticks_at_rate(reference_ticks: int) -> int`: A setting counted in ticks at the reference rate (60 a second) as ticks at this match's rate, so it lasts the same time: round(ticks
  × rate ÷ 60), at least 1 if the setting is above 0; 0 and negative come back unchanged. An 8-tick wind-up is 4 ticks at 30.
- `per_tick_at_rate(reference_amount: float) -> float`: An amount added each tick at the reference rate (sight's fill_rate, say) as the amount each tick adds at this match's rate:
  amount × 60 ÷ rate.
- `get_tick_dt() -> float`: Length of one tick in seconds.
- `get_physics_factor() -> float`: Multiply velocity by this before move_and_slide (and divide after), which scales by Godot's physics delta, so a tick moves the pawn
  velocity × tick length even if tick_rate isn't the physics rate. 1.0 when they match.
- `get_interpolation_fraction() -> float`: How far between the last tick and the next it is, 0 to 1. For smoothing visuals per rendered frame.
- `seconds_to_ticks(seconds: float) -> int`: Seconds (as designers type them) to whole ticks. Any time above zero is at least one tick, so a short window never becomes zero.
- `ticks_to_seconds(ticks: int) -> float`: Ticks to seconds at this match's rate.
- `set_tick(new_tick: int) -> void`: Jumps to a tick number; the only way to change `tick`. For a client setting its clock from the server's. Not allowed during a tick
  or a replay. Saved history stays valid, as each slot remembers which tick it holds.
- `is_resimulating() -> bool`: True while a rollback replays ticks. Cosmetic effects (sounds, particles) must not fire then.
- `is_in_tick() -> bool`: True while a tick runs, from before_tick to after_tick. A request aimed at another pawn's AI made then is queued for that pawn's next
  AI step (pawn spec 15.1), so it never depends on which pawn went first.
- `is_in_simulate() -> bool`: True while a tick's simulate phase runs (not a replay's). An effect aimed at another entity then is queued and delivered from
  `after_simulate` (pawn spec 15.1).
- `tick_rng(key: int, salt: int = 0) -> RandomNumberGenerator`: Repeatable randomness for gameplay, instead of randf(): the rolls depend only on key (usually an entity id), tick and salt (separates
  rolls in one tick), so a replayed tick rolls the same. Use it at once; the same object is returned every call.
- `rollback(from_tick: int) -> bool`: Rolls predicted participants back to how they ended from_tick, then replays every tick up to the last finished one (netcode spec 3.5).
  Only between ticks or from before_tick; else warns and returns false, as it does if nothing could load or from_tick is in the future. Rules in the README.
- `_load_for_rollback(from_tick: int) -> Array`: Loads resimulated participants, then following ones near them (far-away followers are skipped, which keeps a swarm affordable).
  Empty if no resimulated participant could load.
- `_commit(t: int) -> void`: The commit: every active entity's row for this tick into the store, in one pass. Entities the store can't read by itself (still
  being matched, or a node gone) are handed to their owner's `_store_gather(handle, tick)`.
- `_sync_collision_world() -> void`: Brings every body's collision up to date between two ticks of one frame. One body alone never collides with itself, so this only
  matters for two or more.
- `reset_profile() -> void`: Empties the timing record. See `profile_enabled`.
- `is_authority() -> bool`: True where gameplay outcomes are decided. Offline: always. Online: the server.
- `get_match_options() -> PackedStringArray`: The settings a start menu may offer before a match (MatchOptionsPanel.add_from_autoloads): the load ladder.
- `_lower_step_fits() -> bool`: True if the next step down looks safe now: load under `lower_below`, or the predicted load for the lower step (load now plus
  what this step saved, or twice the load if unknown) under `raise_above` less `step_down_headroom`.
- `_profile_phase(phase: StringName, mark: int) -> int`: Adds the time since mark to this phase, and returns the new mark.
- `_rebuild_phases() -> void`: Sorts participants and splits them by the phase methods they have. Only runs when the registry changed. Also drops freed participants.
